newsitem.title: CANADA: NBA BASKETBALL-FITZSIMMONS STEPPING ASIDE FOR AINGE AS SUNS COACH.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-FITZSIMMONS STEPPING ASIDE FOR AINGE AS SUNS COACH.

text.p: Cotton Fitzsimmons made Thursday night's game at Vancouver his last as coach of the Phoenix Suns, turning over the reins to assistant Danny Ainge.

Ainge was hired as an assistant May 30 to replace Fitzsimmons after this season. But Phoenix came into the game 0-7 -- its worst start in nine years -- and Fitzsimmons was frustrated with the team's play.
"Tonight will be my last game to coach in the NBA," Fitzsimmons said in a statement issued by the team.

"I have made the decision to turn this club over to Danny Ainge. Our game plan was to relinquish the coaching duties to Danny at the end of the season. This was something we had tried and done successfully in the past. Unfortunately, it was not working this time."
It was believed to be the earliest NBA coaching change in a season since Gene Shue was fired by the Philadelphia 76ers six games into the 1977-78 season.

At 65, Fitzsimmons was the oldest coach in the NBA. He came down from the front office last season to replace Paul Westphal, who was fired on January 16. Westphal served as an assistant to Fitzsimmons before taking over as coach in 1992.
Fitzsimmons will take another position in the organisation. He already has served as director of player personnel, broadcaster and three stints as coach.
"I have total confidence in Danny Ainge, the staff and the players to get the job done," Fitzsimmons said.
"I will always be available to provide any input to the coaching staff and players and will now devote my time and energy to the continued improvement and success of the Phoenix Suns franchise."

In a coaching career that began in 1970, Fitzsimmons compiled a record of 832-774, placing him seventh on the all-time victory list. He won Coach of the Year Awards in 1979 with Kansas City and 1989 with Phoenix.

The Suns traded All-Star forward Charles Barkley during the off-season and Fitzsimmons installed a triple-post offence similar to the one used by the NBA champion Chicago Bulls. But the early results were not as good as the Bulls'.
Ainge's first game will be Sunday night at home against the Los Angeles Lakers.
Ainge, a 14-year NBA veteran with four teams, will have former NBA forward Paul Silas and Donn Nelson as assistants. He played in six NBA Finals, winning championships with Boston in 1984 and 1986.
The 36-year-old Ainge left his position as a television analyst to take the job with the Suns. Before his basketball career, Ainge played baseball for the Toronto Blue Jays.
